quests.name: The Score
quests.summary: Take the aptitude battery and sign with open eyes.

stages.objective: Review deployment and custody consequences with Dana.
Complete 12 timed verbal, mechanical, spatial, and arithmetic questions.
Choose an enlistment term and read the casualty-risk language before signing.

choice.text: Take the paperwork back to Dana.

quests.name: Buzzcut
quests.summary: Complete three game days of basic training without confusing noise for purpose.

stages.objective: Report to Staff Sgt. Vance and surrender prohibited inventory for storage.
Complete timed crawl, wall, balance, and carry inputs. Discipline can recover one miss per tier.
Pass barracks inspection or own the error without blaming a squadmate.
Choose one starting role based on aptitude: logistics, communications, driver, or security.

quests.name: Allotment
quests.summary: Make child support leave your pay before any other choice can reach it.

stages.objective: Meet the finance clerk and choose 10, 20, or 28 percent of base pay.
Choose whether the allotment can be paused during hardship.

choice.text: Set 20 percent with a hardship pause.

stages.objective: Receive the first pay stub with the transfer already gone.
stages.dialogue: Petty: Best money I spend is money I never get to improvise with.

quests.name: First Rotation
quests.summary: Run supplies with Petty and Dominguez and learn why squads lower individual risk.

stages.objective: Balance water, medical crates, and fuel within the truck limit.
Choose a washed road or a slower ridge route.

choice.text: Take the ridge and arrive late but intact.
Cross the wash before weather closes it.

stages.objective: Stay with Petty during repair or ride ahead with Dominguez.
Debrief an uneventful mission without pretending uneventful means safe.

quests.name: The Lottery
quests.summary: A visible casualty number sits beside triple pay.

stages.objective: Receive a 3-5 day combat deployment offer generated 14-21 game days after the last rotation.
Review individual casualty odds after Combat, role, and squad-size reductions.
Accept, ask squadmates to deploy together, or decline.

choice.text: Decline and remain for the custody hearing.

quests.name: Contact
quests.summary: An ambush makes squad bonds mechanical, not decorative.

stages.objective: Choose vehicle order after Petty notices disturbed gravel.
React to the disabled third vehicle within one decision window.

choice.text: Lay cover while Dominguez reaches the driver.
Reach the driver yourself while Petty covers.
Secure the medical cargo and hold position.

stages.objective: Order Petty left or Dominguez right based on the earlier route read. Bond reveals the safer call.
stages.casualty: A squadmate can die. The result is seeded and auditable, never silently rerolled.

stages.objective: Sit through the after-action review and choose how to answer 'who called the turn.'

quests.name: Day Ninety
quests.summary: Attend a custody hearing remotely from deployment.

stages.objective: Find a stable video link before the docket calls the case.
Let the allotment and service record count while absence also counts.
Receive an order based on normal factors plus allotment bonus and deployment absence penalty.

quests.name: Terminal Leave
quests.summary: After sixty game days, choose the reliable risk or the uncertain home.

stages.objective: Review honorable-discharge benefits: VA voucher, SRO skip, education perk discount.
Re-up at higher pay and risk, or discharge and go home.
Sign another term with 1.35x pay and 1.2x deployment risk.
Accept the housing voucher and meet {{childName}} at the transit platform.

nodes.text: Recruitment called to verify your address. That is an efficient sentence with several problems inside it.

choices.text: You said I could change paths.

nodes.text: Yes. Friday comes whether the labor lot likes your face or not. An allotment can become your strongest custody evidence.
You can. I said the road changes. I did not say the road waits.
Training takes three game days. Deployments take three to five. Hearings continue. A judge can respect service and count absence in the same breath.

choices.text: The street can kill me too.

nodes.text: True. The Army puts the odds in a box. The street leaves them in the weather.
I would distrust anyone who answered that for you, including me.
Set the allotment before the first paycheck. If you wait to feel rich, the money will find a louder need.
Recruits, place civilian bags on the line. Contraband includes alcohol, blades, and confidence unsupported by evidence.
Photograph stays with you. If it motivates you, good. If it distracts you, learn the difference before an engine does.
Staff Sergeant. The extra word was earned through paperwork and knee pain.
Bunk twelve. Make the bed square enough to offend nature. Formation in nine minutes, which is eight minutes after I stop explaining nine.
This corner is folded like it has legal counsel. Who made the bed?
Correct answer. Incorrect bed. One can improve before lunch.
Did Petty also move your hands? Fascinating. Both of you remake it until causality is established.
Submit a maintenance request to gravity. While it processes, remake the bed.
Water, medical, fuel. Truck says we can bring two and a half. Dominguez says the truck is a pessimist.

nodes.speaker: Corporal Mateo Dominguez
nodes.text: The truck is a realist. Petty thinks optimism changes axle ratings.

nodes.speaker: Corporal Mateo Dominguez
nodes.text: People forgive late fuel. They do not drink apologies. Put water back.

nodes.speaker: Specialist Imani Petty
nodes.text: Excellent. We will whisper encouragement to the suspension.

nodes.speaker: Specialist Imani Petty
nodes.text: Look at us, compromising before sunrise. Civilization survives another hour.
Gravel ahead has tire marks over our tire marks. Somebody visited while we were at checkpoint two.

choices.text: Move our vehicle to the rear.

nodes.speaker: Corporal Mateo Dominguez
nodes.text: Rear watches the turn but loses the radio relay. Acceptable if Petty rides with you.

nodes.speaker: Corporal Mateo Dominguez
nodes.text: Ten vehicle lengths. If this is nothing, we lose a minute. Minutes are cheap today.

nodes.speaker: Specialist Imani Petty
nodes.text: Stopping makes us a very organized target. Slow, spread, watch the left cut.

variants.all-survive: Everybody returned. That changes the report, not the question. Who called the turn?
variants.petty-dead: Petty did not return. The report needs sequence, not tribute. Who called the turn?
variants.dominguez-dead: Dominguez did not return. We will say his name after we get the order right. Who called the turn?

nodes.text: Then describe what you knew when you called it. Do not borrow knowledge from the outcome.

choices.text: Describe the disturbed gravel, radio call, and choice.

nodes.text: A squad can share a decision. The report cannot. Start with the first voice.
That may be true. Sit with it until you can separate missing memory from a memory you dislike.
Guilt is not a map back through the event. Use the map we have. Sleep when they release you.
The connection is unstable. The record, unfortunately, is clear.

choices.text: I can hear you, Your Honor.

variants.locked: The irrevocable allotment has arrived every pay period. It is the strongest income evidence before this court.
variants.flexible: The allotment has arrived regularly, with one hardship pause.

nodes.text: You have also missed two in-person visits due to deployment. Service explains absence. It does not convert absence into presence.
I did not call it simple. I called it a factor.
What should {{childName}} understand about why you are not in this room?

choices.text: That I chose steady money and accepted the cost.
That I am trying to come home with something solid.
That I may have chosen wrong for a reason that was real.

nodes.text: The court will not edit that answer. It will be included as given.
Sixty days. The Army offers another term because you became expensive to replace. Home offers no such compliment.
Thirty-five percent more base pay. Promotion track restored. Twenty percent more deployment exposure. The numbers are honest and incomplete.
Honorable discharge, VA voucher that skips the SRO wait, education discount, and the opportunity to discover whether you can live without a formation telling you when morning starts.
Then sign once. Nobody gets more committed by pressing harder.
nodes.stage: Vance signs below you. Petty or Dominguez waits outside with coffee and does not ask whether it was the right choice.

nodes.text: Turn in your field gear. Keep the photograph. It was never ours.
nodes.stage: At the Halvern platform, {{childName}} stands beside Dana. They see you before the train stops and lift one hand, the same almost-wave from the first visit. This time you have time to answer it.

events.effect: permanent character death and Honor ending trigger
VA voucher and education perk discount
